title: J.X: Partly for Philippica fame — Reformed hold Melanchthon's name with Luther's; do not sneer at anti-idolatry Reformers as heretics
pass_a_gloss: Meanwhile they have been disputed partly for the favor of Philippica fame, which the Reformed hold in delight equally with Luther's, judging that this favor is owed to all the Reformers of pontifical idol-madness, lest the writings and deeds of those men be either rashly sneered at, or odiously harassed and convicted of heresy;
pass_b_english: Meantime the case was argued partly for Philippica fame, which the Reformed cherish as they do Luther's.
They reckon that favor owed to every Reformer who broke with papal idol-madness: do not rashly sneer at their writings and deeds, nor bait them as heretics.
source_text: Disputata interim sunt partim in gratiam Philippicae famae, quam perinde atque Lutheri, in deliciis habent Reformati, omnibus Reformatoribus Pontificiae Idolomaniae hanc gratiam deberi augurati, ne Scripta Factaque istorum vel temere suggillentur, vel exagitentur odiose haereseosque coarguantur;
